title: Points on the Coordinate Plane
short: Go across by x, then up by y.
trouble: Children swap the coordinates, plotting (2, 5) at (5, 2).

blocks.html: You have placed numbers on a number line. Put two number lines together, one across and one up, crossing at 0, and every point on a flat grid gets its own address. That is the coordinate plane.

An ordered pair $(x, y)$ tells you how to reach a point from the origin $(0, 0)$: go $x$ units across along the x-axis, then $y$ units up. The order matters: $(2, 5)$ and $(5, 2)$ are different points.

One number line can only describe positions along a line. A flat grid needs two directions, so a point needs two numbers. Everyone agrees to give the across number first and the up number second, so an ordered pair means the same point to everyone.

blocks.name: g5-grid
blocks.cap: Drag the red point (or use the arrow keys) to $(2, 5)$. Press “Show the path” to see the trip: across first, then up.

blocks.title: Plot a point
steps: The first number is 4: go 4 units right along the x-axis.
The second number is 3: go 3 units up. Mark the point.

blocks.title: Read a point
blocks.q: A point is 6 units right of the origin and 1 unit up. What are its coordinates?

blocks.name: g5-grid
blocks.cap: $A = (2, 5)$ and $B = (5, 2)$ use the same numbers in a different order, so they are different points.

blocks.html: Swapping the coordinates and plotting $(2, 5)$ at $(5, 2)$. Remember “across, then up,” like walking along a hallway before taking the stairs. Check: the first number should match the x-axis below the point.
